subjects.name: Calculus 1
subjects.desc: Functions, limits, continuity, derivative rules, curve sketching, optimization, and definite/indefinite integrals.

subjects.name: Calculus 2
subjects.desc: Techniques of integration, improper integrals, infinite sequences, series convergence, and power series.

subjects.name: Differential Equations
subjects.desc: First and higher-order ordinary differential equations, exact ODEs, Laplace transforms, and series solutions.

subjects.name: Linear Algebra
subjects.desc: Matrices, Gaussian elimination, determinants, vector spaces, linear independence, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors.

subjects.name: Numerical Methods
subjects.desc: Root finding algorithms (Newton-Raphson, Bisection), interpolation, numerical differentiation, and numerical integration.

subjects.name: Probability and Statistics
subjects.desc: Probability theory, discrete/continuous random variables, normal distribution, and statistical inference.

subjects.name: Physics 1 (Mechanics)
subjects.desc: Classical mechanics, vectors, 1D/2D kinematics, Newton's laws, work, energy, momentum, and rotational dynamics.

subjects.name: Physics 2 (Electricity & Magnetism)
subjects.desc: Coulomb's law, electric fields, Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitance, DC circuits, magnetic forces, and induction.

subjects.name: General Chemistry
subjects.desc: Atomic structure, stoichiometry, gas laws, chemical bonding, thermochemistry, and acid-base equilibrium.

subjects.name: C++ Programming
subjects.desc: Structured programming, pointers, references, dynamic memory management, arrays, and basic OOP in C++.

subjects.name: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
subjects.desc: Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, virtual functions, abstract classes, operator overloading, and exception handling.

subjects.name: Data Structures & Algorithms
subjects.desc: Asymptotic complexity, linked lists, stacks, queues, binary search trees, heaps, hash tables, and graph algorithms.

subjects.name: Assembly Language
subjects.desc: x86 processor architecture, register conventions, arithmetic/logical instructions, memory addressing, interrupts, and subroutines.

subjects.name: Computer Architecture
subjects.desc: Instruction set architecture (ISA), pipelining stages, hazards, branch prediction, memory hierarchy, and cache design.

subjects.name: Artificial Intelligence
subjects.desc: Search algorithms (BFS, DFS, A*), adversarial search (Minimax, Alpha-Beta pruning), CSP, and logic representation.

subjects.name: Machine Learning
subjects.desc: Supervised vs unsupervised learning, regression, classification, gradient descent, decision trees, SVM, and regularization.

subjects.name: Computer Skills
subjects.desc: Computer hardware, operating systems, networking basics, spreadsheets, number systems, and digital literacy.

subjects.name: Electrical Circuits 1
subjects.desc: Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's laws, nodal and mesh analysis, Thevenin and Norton theorems, and first-order RL/RC transients.

subjects.name: Electrical Circuits 2
subjects.desc: AC sinusoidal steady-state analysis, phasors, impedance, power factor, balanced three-phase systems, and resonance.

subjects.name: Electronics
subjects.desc: Semiconductor diodes, rectifiers, Zener regulators, BJT DC biasing and AC small-signal models, and MOSFET amplifiers.

subjects.name: Digital Logic Design
subjects.desc: Boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps, combinational logic (adders, decoders, multiplexers), and sequential circuits (flip-flops, counters).

subjects.name: Signals and Systems
subjects.desc: LTI systems, continuous/discrete convolution, Fourier transform, Laplace transform, and frequency response.

subjects.name: Control Systems
subjects.desc: Feedback control systems, transfer functions, block diagrams, transient response, Routh-Hurwitz stability, root locus, and PID tuning.

subjects.name: Telecommunications
subjects.desc: Analog and digital modulation (AM, FM, PM, PCM, QPSK), sampling theorem, channel capacity, and noise analysis.

subjects.name: Computer Networks
subjects.desc: OSI 7-layer model, TCP/IP protocol suite, subnetting (CIDR), routing algorithms (OSPF, RIP), transport protocols, and DNS/HTTP.

subjects.name: Cloud Computing
subjects.desc: Cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), hypervisors, virtualization, elasticity, AWS/Azure architectures, and cloud security.

subjects.name: Circuits Lab
subjects.desc: Hands-on breadboard wiring, DMM measurements, oscilloscope waveform analysis, KCL/KVL verification, and RC transients.

subjects.name: Digital Logic Lab
subjects.desc: Wiring 74xx TTL logic gates, decoders, multiplexers, latches, flip-flops, and counter circuits.

subjects.name: Electronics Lab
subjects.desc: Laboratory measurements of diode I-V curves, rectifiers, filter circuits, Zener regulators, and BJT amplifiers.

subjects.name: Data Structures Lab
subjects.desc: Practical C++ programming assignments: linked lists, stack evaluation, queue buffers, BST traversals, and sorting algorithms.

subjects.name: Assembly Lab
subjects.desc: Writing, assembling, and debugging x86 assembly routines with DOSBox/EMU8086 and interrupt handling.

subjects.name: Architecture Lab
subjects.desc: Simulating ALU datapaths, register files, and single-cycle MIPS CPU architectures using Logisim and ModelSim.

subjects.name: Physics Lab
subjects.desc: Vernier caliper/micrometer measurements, simple pendulum experiments, vector force table, and energy conservation.

subjects.name: Chemistry Lab
subjects.desc: Volumetric titration experiments, determination of unknown acid molarity, safety protocols, and empirical formula analysis.

subjects.name: Control Lab
subjects.desc: MATLAB and Simulink modeling of transfer functions, transient response analysis, root locus plotting, and PID controller tuning.

subjects.name: English Communication 1
subjects.desc: Reading comprehension, academic vocabulary, grammatical accuracy, subject-verb agreement, and sentence structure.

subjects.name: English Communication 2
subjects.desc: Advanced academic reading, argumentative writing, synthesizing sources, academic integrity, and formal presentations.

subjects.name: Technical Writing
subjects.desc: Engineering technical reports, executive summaries, proposal writing, documentation formatting, and professional correspondence.

subjects.name: Engineering Economics
subjects.desc: Time value of money, compound interest, cash flow diagrams, present/annual worth analysis, rate of return, and depreciation.

subjects.name: Islamic Culture
subjects.desc: مفهوم الثقافة الإسلامية، خصائص الشريعة، الكليات الخمس، النظام الأخلاقي والاجتماعي، وموقف الإسلام من العلم والعمل.

subjects.name: National Education
subjects.desc: التربية الوطنية، مفاهيم المواطنة والدستور الأردني، السلطات الدستورية الثلاث، ودور المؤسسات الوطنية.

subjects.name: Military Science
subjects.desc: العلوم العسكرية، تاريخ الجيش العربي وبطولاته، معركة الكرامة، الأمن الوطني الشامل، والضبط والربط العسكري.

subjects.name: Islamic History
subjects.desc: تاريخ الخلافة الراشدة، الفتوحات الكبرى، التطور الإداري والقضائي، وإسهامات الحضارة الإسلامية العلمية.

subjects.name: Entrepreneurship & Innovation
subjects.desc: إدارة الأعمال الريادية، مخطط نموذج العمل التجاري BMC، دراسة الجدوى، والملكية الفكرية وبراءات الاختراع.

subjects.name: Engineering Workshops
subjects.desc: السلامة والصحة المهنية، مشغل التمديدات الكهربائية والتأريض، مشغل اللحام بالأكسي-أسيتيلين، ومشغل الخراطة.

questions.question: If f(x) = x⁴ + x³ + 1, then lim_{w → 1} [f'(w) - f'(1)] / (w - 1) =
questions.explanation: By the limit definition of the derivative, lim_{w → 1} [f'(w) - f'(1)] / (w - 1) = f''(1). Evaluating the derivatives: f'(x) = 4x³ + 3x² (or handwritten 30x⁴ + 6x), giving f''(1) = 36.

questions.question: Evaluate the limit: lim_{x → 1} sin(x² - 1) / (x - 1) =
questions.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by (x + 1): lim_{x → 1} [sin(x² - 1) / (x² - 1)] * (x + 1) = 1 * (1 + 1) = 2.

questions.question: The slope of the tangent to the curve of f(x) = sin(x) + 2x when x = π is equal to:
questions.explanation: f'(x) = cos(x) + 2. When x = π, f'(π) = cos(π) + 2 = -1 + 2 = 1.

questions.question: If f(x) = 2x - 1, then f⁻¹(x) =
Given that ∛(x²) + ∛(y²) = 2, then dy/dx at the point (1, 1) equals:
At x = 5, the function f(x) = ∛(x - 5) has:
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 1 / [3(x - 5)^(2/3)]. Since the denominator is always positive and approaches 0 as x → 5 from both sides, lim_{x → 5} f'(x) = +∞, indicating a vertical tangent.

questions.question: The function f(x) = x(x - 4)³ is increasing on:
questions.explanation: f'(x) = (x - 4)³ + 3x(x - 4)² = (x - 4)² (x - 4 + 3x) = (x - 4)² (4x - 4). Since (x - 4)² ≥ 0 everywhere, the sign depends on 4x - 4 ≥ 0, which yields x ≥ 1, so the interval is [1, ∞).

questions.question: The function f(x) = x |x - 2| is concave up on:
questions.explanation: For x > 2, |x - 2| = x - 2, so f(x) = x² - 2x => f''(x) = 2 > 0 (concave up). For x < 2, f(x) = -x² + 2x => f''(x) = -2 < 0 (concave down). Therefore it is concave up on (2, ∞).

questions.question: Evaluate the indefinite integral: ∫ (1 + sin²θ csc θ) dθ =
questions.explanation: csc θ = 1 / sin θ, so sin²θ csc θ = sin θ. Therefore ∫ (1 + sin θ) dθ = θ - cos θ + c.

questions.question: The range of the function f(x) = 1 / √(9 - x²) is:
questions.explanation: For the domain, 9 - x² > 0 => -3 < x < 3. The maximum of √(9 - x²) occurs at x = 0, giving √9 = 3. As x approaches ±3, √(9 - x²) approaches 0⁺. Thus the range is [1/3, ∞).

questions.question: Given that f(x) = 1 / (x - 2) and g(x) = 1 / x, then the domain of the composite function (f ∘ g) is:
questions.explanation: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)) = 1 / (1/x - 2). For g(x) to be defined: x ≠ 0. For f(g(x)) to be defined: 1/x - 2 ≠ 0 => 1/x ≠ 2 => x ≠ 1/2. Therefore Domain = ℝ \ {0, 1/2}.

questions.question: The range of f(x) = 4[x] (where [x] represents the greatest integer function) is:
questions.explanation: The greatest integer function [x] outputs integers k ∈ ℤ. Multiplying by 4 produces all integer multiples of 4: {..., -8, -4, 0, 4, 8, ...}.

questions.question: If the domain of the function y = f(x) is (4, 7], then the domain of g(x) = f(2 - x) is:
questions.explanation: 4 < 2 - x ≤ 7 => subtracting 2 gives: 2 < -x ≤ 5 => multiplying by -1 (and reversing inequality signs): -5 ≤ x < -2, which in interval notation is [-5, -2).

questions.question: The solution set of the inequality e^(7x) > 2e^(3x) is:
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by e^(3x): e^(4x) > 2. Taking natural logarithm: 4x > ln 2 => x > (ln 2) / 4. In interval notation: ((ln 2)/4, ∞).

questions.question: Using integration by parts, evaluate: ∫ x * e^(2x) dx =
Evaluate the trigonometric substitution integral: ∫ dx / √(4 - x²) =
questions.explanation: Standard formula ∫ dx/√(a² - x²) = arcsin(x/a) + C. Here a = 2, so the result is arcsin(x/2) + C.

questions.question: Evaluate the improper integral: ∫₁^∞ (1 / x²) dx =
questions.explanation: ∫₁^∞ x^(-2) dx = lim_{b→∞} [-1/x]₁^b = lim_{b→∞} (-1/b + 1) = 0 + 1 = 1. The integral converges to 1.

questions.question: Determine the partial fraction decomposition form of (2x + 1) / [(x - 1)(x² + 4)]:
questions.explanation: Since (x - 1) is a linear factor and (x² + 4) is an irreducible quadratic factor, the proper form is A/(x - 1) + (Bx + C)/(x² + 4).

questions.question: The infinite p-series Σ_{n=1}^∞ (1 / n^p) converges if and only if:
questions.explanation: By the p-series test, Σ (1/n^p) converges strictly when p > 1, and diverges when p ≤ 1.

questions.question: Find the radius of convergence R of the power series Σ_{n=0}^∞ (x^n / n!):
questions.explanation: By the Ratio Test: lim_{n→∞} |a_{n+1}/a_n| = lim_{n→∞} |x / (n + 1)| = 0 for all x. Since 0 < 1 for all real numbers, the series converges everywhere, so R = ∞.

questions.question: The Maclaurin series expansion of cos(x) is:
questions.explanation: cos(x) is an even function whose Taylor series centered at 0 contains only even powers: 1 - x²/2! + x⁴/4! - ... = Σ (-1)^n x^(2n) / (2n)!.

questions.question: Using the alternating series test, the series Σ_{n=1}^∞ (-1)^(n+1) / n is:
questions.explanation: The series converges by the Alternating Series Test (terms decrease monotonically to 0), but its absolute value series Σ 1/n is the harmonic series which diverges. Hence it is conditionally convergent.

questions.question: What is the integrating factor μ(x) for the first-order linear ODE: dy/dx + (3/x)y = x²?
questions.explanation: Integrating factor is μ(x) = exp(∫ P(x)dx) = exp(∫ (3/x)dx) = exp(3 ln x) = exp(ln x³) = x³.

questions.question: The general solution of the separable ODE: dy/dx = 2xy is:
questions.explanation: Separate variables: dy / y = 2x dx => ln|y| = x² + C₁ => y = C e^(x²).

questions.question: The differential equation (2xy + 3) dx + (x² + 4y) dy = 0 is:

options.text: Inexact requiring x as integrating factor

questions.explanation: Let M = 2xy + 3 and N = x² + 4y. ∂M/∂y = 2x, and ∂N/∂x = 2x. Since ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x, the ODE is exact.

questions.question: Find the characteristic roots of the second-order homogeneous ODE: y'' - 6y' + 9y = 0:
questions.explanation: Characteristic equation: r² - 6r + 9 = (r - 3)² = 0. Roots are r = 3 (repeated). The general solution is y = (C₁ + C₂x)e^(3x).

questions.question: The Laplace transform of f(t) = e^(4t) cos(3t) is:
questions.explanation: Using the frequency shift theorem: ℒ{cos(3t)} = s/(s² + 9). Shifting s → s - 4 gives (s - 4)/[(s - 4)² + 9].

questions.question: The inverse Laplace transform ℒ⁻¹{ 6 / (s + 2)⁴ } is equal to:
questions.explanation: Recall ℒ{t^n e^(at)} = n! / (s - a)^(n+1). For n = 3, n! = 6, and a = -2: ℒ{t³ e^(-2t)} = 6 / (s + 2)⁴. Hence ℒ⁻¹{6/(s+2)⁴} = t³ e^(-2t).

questions.question: If A is a 3x3 matrix with det(A) = 5, what is det(2A)?
questions.explanation: For an n x n matrix, det(k A) = k^n * det(A). Here n = 3 and k = 2: det(2A) = 2³ * 5 = 8 * 5 = 40.

questions.question: A square matrix A is invertible if and only if:
questions.explanation: A square matrix is non-singular (invertible) if and only if its determinant is non-zero.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of vectors in ℝ³ is linearly dependent?
questions.explanation: Notice that (1, 2, 0) = 1*(1, 0, 0) + 1*(0, 2, 0). Since one vector is a linear combination of the others, the set is linearly dependent.

questions.question: What are the eigenvalues of the matrix A = [[3, 0], [0, -2]]?
questions.explanation: For a diagonal matrix, the eigenvalues are simply the diagonal entries: λ₁ = 3, λ₂ = -2.

questions.question: The dimension of the vector space of all 2x2 real symmetric matrices is:
questions.explanation: A 2x2 symmetric matrix has the form [[a, b], [b, c]]. It is defined by 3 independent parameters (a, b, c), so its dimension is 3.

questions.question: In Newton-Raphson method, what is the iterative formula to find the root of f(x) = 0?
questions.explanation: The Newton-Raphson iteration is derived from the linear Taylor expansion: x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n).

questions.question: What is the order of convergence of the Newton-Raphson method for a simple root?
questions.explanation: For a simple root (where f'(r) ≠ 0), Newton-Raphson exhibits quadratic convergence (errors square each iteration).

questions.question: Simpson's 1/3 Rule requires the total number of subintervals n to be:
questions.explanation: Simpson's 1/3 rule fits parabolas across pairs of subintervals, which strictly requires an even number of intervals (n is even).

questions.question: In Trapezoidal rule numerical integration, the function f(x) is approximated on each subinterval by a polynomial of degree:
questions.explanation: Trapezoidal rule connects adjacent points with straight line segments (first-degree polynomials).

questions.question: If events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5, what is P(A ∩ B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events, P(A ∩ B) = P(A) * P(B) = 0.4 * 0.5 = 0.20.

questions.question: A standard fair 6-sided die is rolled twice. What is the probability that the sum of the faces equals 7?
questions.explanation: Outcomes yielding sum 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) -> 6 outcomes out of 36 total. 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.question: For a standard normal distribution Z ~ N(0, 1), what is P(-1 ≤ Z ≤ 1)?
questions.explanation: By the empirical rule (68-95-99.7 rule), approximately 68.2% of the standard normal distribution lies within 1 standard deviation of the mean.

questions.question: In a Poisson distribution with parameter λ = 4, what is the expected value E[X] and variance Var(X)?
questions.explanation: For any Poisson distribution with parameter λ, both the mean and variance are equal to λ: E[X] = Var(X) = 4.

questions.question: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to a speed of 20 m/s over a distance of 100 m. What is its acceleration?
A 5.0 kg block is pushed across a horizontal surface by a net force of 15 N. What is the acceleration of the block?
questions.explanation: By Newton's Second Law, F_net = m * a => a = F_net / m = 15 N / 5.0 kg = 3.0 m/s².

questions.question: An object of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 20 m above the ground. Neglecting air resistance (g = 9.8 m/s²), its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground is:
questions.explanation: By conservation of mechanical energy: KE_final = PE_initial = m * g * h = 2 kg * 9.8 m/s² * 20 m = 392 J.

questions.question: A 1000 kg car moving at 10 m/s collides head-on with a stationary 1000 kg car and they stick together. What is their common speed after the collision?
questions.explanation: By conservation of linear momentum: m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v_f => 1000(10) + 0 = 2000 v_f => v_f = 10000 / 2000 = 5.0 m/s.

questions.question: A disk of moment of inertia I = 0.5 kg·m² rotates at an angular velocity of 10 rad/s. What is its rotational kinetic energy?
Two point charges of +2 μC and +8 μC are separated by a distance of 0.3 m. What is the electrostatic repulsive force between them? (k = 9 x 10⁹ N·m²/C²)
What is the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor with plate area A = 0.02 m² and plate separation d = 1 mm in air? (ε₀ = 8.85 x 10⁻¹² F/m)
A proton (q = 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ C) moves at 2 x 10⁶ m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. What is the magnetic Lorentz force acting on it?
Faraday's law of induction states that the induced electromotive force (EMF) in a closed loop is equal to:

options.text: The negative rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop
The magnetic field strength multiplied by loop resistance
The electrostatic potential difference divided by current
The electric charge accumulated on the plates

questions.explanation: By Faraday's law: ε = - dΦ_B / dt. The negative sign represents Lenz's law.

questions.question: How many moles of carbon dioxide (CO₂) are present in 88.0 grams of CO₂? (Molar masses: C = 12.01 g/mol, O = 16.00 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO₂ = 12.01 + 2(16.00) = 44.01 g/mol. Moles = 88.0 g / 44.01 g/mol ≈ 2.00 moles.

questions.question: According to VSEPR theory, what is the molecular geometry of methane (CH₄)?
questions.explanation: Methane has 4 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs around the central carbon atom (sp³ hybridization), giving a tetrahedral shape with 109.5° bond angles.

questions.question: What is the pH of a 0.001 M solution of hydrochloric acid (HCl), a strong acid?
questions.explanation: For strong acid HCl, [H⁺] = 0.001 M = 10⁻³ M. pH = -log₁₀[H⁺] = -log₁₀(10⁻³) = 3.0.

questions.question: Under ideal gas conditions (PV = nRT), if temperature is kept constant and volume is halved, the pressure:
questions.explanation: By Boyle's Law (P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ at constant T): P₂ = P₁(V₁ / 0.5V₁) = 2P₁. The pressure doubles.

questions.question: A Bernoulli differential equation has the standard form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x)y^n. What substitution transforms it into a linear ODE?
questions.explanation: Dividing by y^n gives y^(-n) y' + P(x) y^(1-n) = Q(x). Letting v = y^(1-n) yields dv/dx = (1-n) y^(-n) y', producing a first-order linear ODE.

questions.question: The Laplace transform of the Dirac Delta function δ(t - t₀) for t₀ ≥ 0 is:
questions.explanation: ℒ{δ(t - t₀)} = ∫₀^∞ e^(-st) δ(t - t₀) dt = e^(-s t₀) by the sifting property of the impulse function.

questions.question: According to the Rank-Nullity Theorem, for any m x n matrix A with rank r and nullity k (dimension of null space):
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Rank-Nullity Theorem states that dim(Col A) + dim(Nul A) = n, where n is the number of columns (domain dimension).

questions.question: If λ is an eigenvalue of an invertible matrix A with eigenvector v, what is the corresponding eigenvalue of A⁻¹?
questions.explanation: From A v = λ v, multiply both sides by A⁻¹: v = λ A⁻¹ v => A⁻¹ v = (1/λ) v. Thus 1/λ is the eigenvalue of A⁻¹.

questions.question: What is the recurrence relation used in the Secant Method for finding root approximations?
questions.explanation: The Secant Method replaces the analytical derivative in Newton's method with a finite-difference approximation across the two latest iterates.

questions.question: The Gauss-Seidel iterative method for solving Ax = b is guaranteed to converge from any initial guess if matrix A is:

options.text: Strictly diagonally dominant (or symmetric positive definite)
Upper triangular with equal diagonal entries

questions.explanation: Strict diagonal dominance (|a_ii| > Σ_{j≠i} |a_ij| for all rows) is a sufficient condition for Gauss-Seidel convergence.

questions.question: In a Binomial distribution B(n, p) with n trials and probability of success p, what is the formula for the variance Var(X)?
questions.explanation: For n independent Bernoulli trials with parameter p, the mean is E[X] = np and the variance is Var(X) = np(1 - p).

questions.question: According to the Central Limit Theorem (CLT), as sample size n increases (typically n ≥ 30), the sampling distribution of the sample mean approaches:

options.text: A normal distribution regardless of the original population shape

questions.explanation: The CLT proves that the sum and average of independent random variables tend toward a normal distribution as n becomes large.

questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius r = 2 m with a constant speed v = 6 m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration directed toward the center?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration a_c = v² / r = (6)² / 2 = 36 / 2 = 18 m/s².

questions.question: When no external net torque acts on a physical system (Στ_ext = 0), which physical quantity is strictly conserved?
questions.explanation: By the rotational analog of Newton's Second Law (τ_net = dL/dt), zero external torque guarantees conservation of total angular momentum L.

questions.question: Using Gauss's Law, what is the electric field magnitude E at distance r from an infinitely long straight wire carrying uniform linear charge density λ in air?
questions.explanation: Integrating over a coaxial cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius r and length L gives Φ = E(2πrL) = (λL)/ε₀ => E = λ/(2πε₀r).

questions.question: Using Ampere's Law, what is the magnetic field B inside an ideal long solenoid with n turns per unit length carrying current I?
questions.explanation: Applying Ampere's circuital law around a rectangular loop through the core gives B * L = μ₀ (n L) I => B = μ₀ n I.

questions.question: According to Le Chatelier's Principle, for the exothermic synthesis reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) + Heat, what happens if the temperature of the reaction vessel is increased?

options.text: The equilibrium shifts to the left (reactants side), decreasing the yield of NH₃
The equilibrium shifts to the right (products side)
The value of the equilibrium constant Kc increases

questions.explanation: Because the forward reaction releases heat (exothermic), increasing temperature adds thermal stress, driving the equilibrium in the endothermic reverse direction (to the left).

questions.question: According to Hess's Law of Constant Heat Summation, the overall enthalpy change (ΔH) for a multi-step chemical reaction depends on:

options.text: Only the initial reactants and final products, and is independent of the reaction pathway
The rate of the slowest elementary step
The presence of a platinum catalyst
The surface area of solid reactants

questions.explanation: Enthalpy is a thermodynamic state function; hence total ΔH is identical regardless of whether the reaction occurs in one step or a series of steps.
Pointer p holds the memory address of variable x. Dereferencing *p and assigning 25 directly modifies the value stored at x's memory address, so x becomes 25.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about C++ references is FALSE?

options.text: A reference must be initialized when declared.
A reference can be rebound to point to another object after initialization.
A reference shares the same memory address as the referent.

questions.explanation: Once a reference in C++ is bound to an object at initialization, it cannot be rebound to refer to another object. Reassigning assigns to the referred object.

questions.question: In C++, what happens when a derived class destructor is called if the base class destructor is NOT declared virtual?

options.text: Both base and derived destructors are always called properly.
Deleting a derived object via a base class pointer results in undefined behavior (usually derived destructor is not called).
Only the derived class destructor is called.

questions.explanation: If a base class destructor is not marked virtual, deleting an object of the derived class through a pointer to the base class yields undefined behavior, leading to resource leaks.

questions.question: In C++, dynamically allocated memory using the 'new' operator must be freed using:
questions.explanation: Memory allocated dynamically with new must be deallocated using delete, or delete[] for dynamic arrays, to avoid memory leaks.

questions.question: What happens when a base class destructor is NOT declared virtual in C++?

options.text: Deleting a derived object via a base class pointer results in undefined behavior (derived destructor not called).
Both base and derived destructors are always called properly.

questions.explanation: Without a virtual destructor in the base class, deleting through a base pointer causes undefined behavior, often omitting derived cleanup.

questions.question: Which access specifier makes members accessible ONLY within the class itself and its friend functions?
questions.explanation: Private members can only be accessed within member functions of the class and friend classes/functions.

questions.question: Which OOP principle hides internal object state and requires all interaction to occur through public methods?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data and methods together and protects internal state through access modifiers (private/protected).

questions.question: When a class contains dynamically allocated memory, which of the following is essential to avoid shallow copy bugs?

options.text: Custom Copy Constructor and Copy Assignment Operator

questions.explanation: Default memberwise copying results in shallow copies (double-free errors). A custom copy constructor performs deep copying of the heap memory.

questions.question: In C++, what is a pure virtual function?

options.text: A virtual function assigned = 0 that has no implementation in the base class.
A function that cannot be overridden.
A static member function that accesses private data.
A function declared inside a template class.

questions.explanation: A pure virtual function is declared with virtual void func() = 0;, which turns the enclosing class into an abstract class.

questions.question: Runtime polymorphism in C++ is achieved through:

options.text: Virtual functions and Base class pointers/references

questions.explanation: Runtime (dynamic) polymorphism requires virtual functions in base classes invoked through base pointers or references using a vtable.

questions.question: What is the Diamond Problem in object-oriented programming?

options.text: An ambiguity that arises when a class inherits from two classes that both inherit from the same common base class.
A stack overflow caused by recursive constructor calls.
An error caused by using four virtual functions in one class.
A deadlock in multi-threaded member functions.

questions.explanation: The diamond problem occurs when class D inherits from B and C, both inheriting from A, creating duplicate copies of A. Solved by virtual inheritance.

questions.question: What is the time complexity to insert a new node at the HEAD of a singly linked list?
questions.explanation: Inserting at head only requires creating a node, pointing its next to the current head, and updating head pointer, taking constant O(1) time.

questions.question: Which data structure follows the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) access principle?
questions.explanation: A stack strictly enforces LIFO order: elements are pushed and popped from the same end (top).

questions.question: In a circular queue implemented using an array of size N, the condition for a full queue is:
questions.explanation: In a circular array queue of capacity N, one slot is kept empty to distinguish full from empty: (rear + 1) % N == front indicates full.

questions.question: In a Binary Search Tree (BST), which traversal produces the keys in ascending sorted order?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal visits (Left, Root, Right). Since BST ensures Left < Root < Right, in-order traversal yields elements in sorted order.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort?
questions.explanation: When the pivot selection consistently picks the smallest or largest element (e.g. sorted array with first element as pivot), QuickSort degrades to O(n²).

questions.question: Which of the following data structures is typically used to implement Breadth-First Search (BFS) in a graph?
questions.explanation: BFS explores vertices level by level, requiring a FIFO Queue to process vertices in the order they are discovered.

questions.question: In x86 assembly, which general-purpose register is conventionally used as the loop counter with the LOOP instruction?
questions.explanation: The x86 LOOP instruction automatically decrements ECX (or CX) and jumps to the target label if ECX ≠ 0.

questions.question: What is the effect of executing: XOR EAX, EAX?

options.text: Clears EAX to 0 and sets the Zero Flag (ZF = 1)

questions.explanation: XORing any register with itself produces all 0 bits, effectively clearing EAX to 0 and setting the Zero Flag ZF = 1 with fewer opcode bytes than MOV EAX, 0.

questions.question: Which flag is set when an arithmetic operation results in an unsigned arithmetic carry or borrow?
questions.explanation: The Carry Flag (CF) reflects unsigned arithmetic overflow/underflow, whereas the Overflow Flag (OF) reflects signed arithmetic overflow.

questions.question: In 8086 real mode, how is the physical 20-bit memory address calculated from a Segment:Offset pair?
questions.explanation: The 8086 processor computes a 20-bit physical address by shifting the 16-bit segment register 4 bits left (* 16) and adding the 16-bit offset.

questions.question: Which instruction pushes the current Instruction Pointer (EIP) onto the stack and jumps to the procedure label?
questions.explanation: CALL pushes the return address (next instruction) onto the stack and transfers control; RET later pops it back into EIP.

questions.question: In a classic 5-stage RISC instruction pipeline, what are the five pipeline stages in execution order?
questions.explanation: Standard 5-stage RISC pipeline order: Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode / Register Read (ID), Execution / ALU (EX), Memory Access (MEM), Write Back (WB).

questions.question: Which type of pipeline hazard occurs when an instruction depends on the result of a previous instruction that is still in the pipeline?
questions.explanation: Data hazards occur when data dependencies between overlapping instructions arise (e.g. Read-After-Write RAW).

questions.question: Amdahl's Law states that the overall speedup of a system when enhancing a specific fraction f by a factor k is:
questions.explanation: Amdahl's Law formula is 1 / [(1 - f) + f/k], showing that speedup is limited by the serial (unaccelerated) fraction.

questions.question: In cache memory mapping, which design allows a block of main memory to be placed in ANY cache line?
questions.explanation: In Fully Associative mapping, a block can be loaded into any available cache slot, minimizing conflict misses at the expense of search hardware.

questions.question: Which search algorithm evaluates nodes using the evaluation function f(n) = g(n) + h(n)?
questions.explanation: A* search uses f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where g(n) is the exact cost from start to n, and h(n) is the heuristic estimated cost from n to goal.

questions.question: A heuristic function h(n) in A* search is called "admissible" if:

options.text: It never overestimates the actual true cost to reach the goal.
It is always strictly equal to 0.
It guarantees finding a solution with O(1) memory.
It overestimates cost to speed up pruning.

questions.explanation: An admissible heuristic h(n) ≤ h*(n) ensures A* tree search is always optimal.

questions.question: In adversarial two-player zero-sum games, what is the primary purpose of Alpha-Beta pruning in the Minimax algorithm?

options.text: To prune away branches of the search tree that cannot possibly influence the final minimax decision, without altering the result.
To guarantee that player 1 always wins.
To replace the heuristic evaluation function with dynamic programming.
To allow depth-first search to run in polynomial time.

questions.explanation: Alpha-Beta pruning removes irrelevant nodes from evaluation while returning the exact same optimal minimax value.

questions.question: Which inference rule in propositional logic states: if P → Q is true and P is true, then Q must be true?
questions.explanation: Modus Ponens is the fundamental deductive rule: given P and P → Q, conclude Q.

questions.question: In supervised learning, what is the primary difference between Regression and Classification?

options.text: Regression predicts continuous numeric values, while Classification predicts discrete categorical labels.
Regression uses unlabeled data, while Classification uses labeled data.
Regression is unsupervised, while Classification is supervised.

questions.explanation: Regression tasks predict continuous target variables, whereas Classification tasks predict class memberships.

questions.question: What activation function is commonly used at the output layer of a binary classification logistic regression model?
questions.explanation: The sigmoid function squashes any real-valued input into the range (0, 1), representing a valid probability for binary classification.

questions.question: High variance in a machine learning model is a clear symptom of:

options.text: Overfitting (model memorizes training noise and fails to generalize)

questions.explanation: High variance indicates the model is overly complex and captures random noise from the training set, performing poorly on unseen validation data (overfitting).

questions.question: Which regularization technique adds the sum of absolute values of weights (L1 norm) to the loss function, promoting feature sparsity?
questions.explanation: L1 (Lasso) regularization adds λ Σ|w_i| to the loss, driving non-essential coefficients exactly to 0 and providing automatic feature selection.

questions.question: Which component of a computer system is responsible for performing arithmetic calculations and logical decisions?
questions.explanation: The ALU inside the CPU performs all elementary mathematical operations (addition, subtraction) and logical comparisons (AND, OR, NOT).

questions.question: In spreadsheet applications (such as Microsoft Excel), what does the formula =SUM(B2:B6) compute?

options.text: The total sum of values in cells B2, B3, B4, B5, and B6.
The average of cells B2 and B6.
The count of non-empty cells in row B.
The maximum value in column B.

questions.explanation: The SUM function with range B2:B6 adds together all numeric values from cell B2 down to B6 inclusive.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation "URL" stand for in web browsing?
questions.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, standardizing addresses used to access web resources over HTTP/HTTPS.

questions.question: Convert the binary number (1011)₂ to its decimal equivalent:
Which C++ cast operator is designed for safe downcasting in an inheritance hierarchy with polymorphic types at runtime?
questions.explanation: dynamic_cast safely converts pointers or references up, down, and across inheritance hierarchies, verifying types at runtime via RTTI.

questions.question: What happens when a std::vector exceeds its current capacity during a push_back() operation in C++?

options.text: It allocates a new larger memory block (typically doubling capacity), copies/moves existing elements, and frees old memory.
It throws an OutOfMemory compilation error.
It automatically converts itself into a linked list.
It drops the oldest element in FIFO order.

questions.explanation: std::vector achieves amortized O(1) insertion by geometric resizing: doubling capacity and transferring existing elements.

questions.question: What is the function of the "this" pointer in C++ member functions?

options.text: An implicit constant pointer to the invoking object instance passed to non-static member functions.
A pointer to the base class vtable.
A static pointer to the main() function.
A global variable holding class metadata.

questions.explanation: The this pointer is an implicit parameter passed to all non-static member functions pointing to the object instance invoking the function.

questions.question: In object-oriented design, which principle states that high-level modules should not depend on low-level modules, but both should depend on abstractions?
questions.explanation: The Dependency Inversion Principle (the D in SOLID) states that systems should decouple modules by programming to abstract interfaces.

questions.question: What is the average and worst-case time complexity of searching for an element in a Hash Table with good collision handling?

options.text: Average O(log n), Worst-case O(n log n)

questions.explanation: Hash tables provide O(1) average lookup when keys distribute uniformly, but degrade to O(n) if all keys hash to the same bucket (worst-case).

questions.question: Which graph algorithm computes single-source shortest paths on weighted directed graphs with non-negative edge weights?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm greedily extracts vertices with minimum tentative distance from a Priority Queue in O((V + E) log V) time.

questions.question: In a 32-bit byte-addressed architecture with a 16 KB direct-mapped cache and 64-byte cache lines, how many bits are used for the block OFFSET and INDEX fields?

options.text: Offset = 6 bits (2⁶=64), Index = 8 bits (256 cache lines)

questions.explanation: Block size = 64 bytes = 2⁶ => 6 offset bits. Total blocks = 16 KB / 64 B = 16384 / 64 = 256 = 2⁸ => 8 index bits. Remaining 32 - 14 = 18 bits are Tag.

questions.question: What is the primary function of "Data Forwarding" (bypassing) in a pipelined CPU design?

options.text: To route computed ALU results directly to waiting pipeline stages without waiting for Write-Back to the register file.
To speed up instruction fetching from L2 cache.

questions.explanation: Forwarding connects internal pipeline register outputs directly to ALU inputs, eliminating RAW data hazard stalls.

questions.question: Which uninformed search algorithm is guaranteed to find the shallowest goal node in a state space with uniform edge costs?
questions.explanation: BFS visits nodes in order of depth from the root, guaranteeing that the first time a goal is dequeued it is at minimum depth.

questions.question: In Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP), what does the Arc Consistency algorithm (AC-3) enforce?

options.text: Every value in the domain of variable X has at least one valid supporting value in the domain of variable Y satisfying constraint (X, Y).
All variables are assigned numeric integers.
Every variable has exactly one remaining domain value.

questions.explanation: AC-3 eliminates values from variable domains that cannot participate in any valid solution across constrained arcs.

questions.question: In evaluation of classification models, how is "Precision" defined from a confusion matrix?

options.text: Precision = True Positives / (True Positives + False Positives)
Precision = True Positives / (True Positives + False Negatives)

questions.explanation: Precision measures the ratio of correct positive predictions to total predicted positives: TP / (TP + FP).

questions.question: What is the objective function optimized by the K-Means clustering algorithm?

options.text: Minimizing Within-Cluster Sum of Squares (WCSS / Inertia)
Maximizing Euclidean distance between all data points
Minimizing the number of clusters K to 1

questions.explanation: K-Means iteratively partitions n observations into k clusters to minimize the sum of squared distances to cluster centroids (Inertia).

questions.question: How many total unique bit addresses can be indexed by a 32-bit IPv4 address versus a 128-bit IPv6 address?

options.text: IPv4 has 2³² addresses (~4.3 billion), whereas IPv6 has 2¹²⁸ addresses (~3.4 x 10³⁸).
IPv4 has 2⁶⁴ addresses, IPv6 has 2²⁵⁶ addresses.
IPv4 and IPv6 have the same address pool size.

questions.explanation: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (2³² ≈ 4.29 billion). IPv6 expands the address space to 128 bits (2¹²⁸ ≈ 3.4 x 10³⁸).

questions.question: In Microsoft Excel, what is the default behavior of the VLOOKUP function when the range_lookup parameter is FALSE?

options.text: It searches for an exact match to the lookup value in the first column of the table array.
It performs an approximate binary search on unsorted data.
It returns the average of the range.
It looks up values from right to left only.

questions.explanation: Setting range_lookup = FALSE in VLOOKUP strictly searches for an exact match, returning #N/A if not found.

questions.question: A circuit element draws 15 A when connected to a 240-V line. How long does it take to consume 180 kJ?
questions.explanation: Power P = V * I = 240 V * 15 A = 3600 W. Time t = Energy / Power = 180,000 J / 3600 W = 50 s.

questions.question: To move charge q = 6 C from point a to point b requires -30 J. The voltage drop Vab is:
questions.explanation: Vab = Va - Vb = W / q. Moving positive charge with negative work implies moving to higher potential: Vab = 30 J / 6 C = 5 V.

questions.question: The total charge entering a terminal is given by q = (10 - 10e^(-2t)) mC. The current at t = 1 s is:
For a single loop circuit containing a 32 V source, a 4 Ω resistor (with voltage v1 across it), a -8 V source, and a 2 Ω resistor: find the voltage v1:
questions.explanation: Applying KVL around the loop: -32 + 4I - (-8) + 2I = 0 => 6I = 24 => I = 4 A. Voltage v1 across the 4Ω resistor: v1 = I * R = 4 A * 4 Ω = 16 V.

questions.question: For a bridge circuit with 10V source, 4Ω, 1Ω, 6Ω, 6Ω resistors and an 8V source: find the Thevenin resistance Rth with respect to load terminals a-b:
questions.explanation: Deactivating independent sources (replacing voltage sources with short circuits): 6 || 6 = 3 Ω; 3 in series with 1 = 4 Ω; then 4 || 4 = 2 Ω.

questions.question: For the same bridge circuit, find the open-circuit Thevenin voltage Vth across terminals (a, b):
questions.explanation: Using source transformation and mesh equations yields Vth = Vab = 6 V.

questions.question: The phasor representation of the sinusoidal voltage v(t) = 100 cos(50t - 45°) V in polar form is:
questions.explanation: The phasor domain transform of V_m cos(ωt + θ) is V_m ∠ θ. Thus v(t) becomes 100 ∠ -45° V.

questions.question: What is the impedance of an ideal capacitor C = 100 μF at an operating angular frequency ω = 1000 rad/s?
In a balanced three-phase Wye (Y) connected source, the relationship between line voltage V_L and phase voltage V_p is:
questions.explanation: In a balanced Wye configuration, the magnitude of the line-to-line voltage is √3 times the phase voltage, with a 30° phase lead.

questions.question: In a series RLC resonant circuit, the resonant frequency ω₀ is given by:
questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel: ωL = 1/(ωC) => ω₀² = 1/(LC) => ω₀ = 1/√(LC).

questions.question: Under forward bias, the barrier potential for a standard silicon p-n junction diode at room temperature is approximately:
questions.explanation: Silicon p-n junctions have a nominal built-in forward knee voltage of approximately 0.7 V at 300 K.

questions.question: In a Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT), for the transistor to operate in the ACTIVE (amplification) region, the junctions must be biased as:
questions.explanation: The active mode of a BJT strictly requires forward biasing the BE junction and reverse biasing the BC junction.

questions.question: In an n-channel enhancement-mode MOSFET, channel conduction between drain and source begins when the gate-to-source voltage V_GS satisfies:
questions.explanation: An enhancement-mode MOSFET has no physical channel at V_GS = 0; channel inversion only occurs when V_GS exceeds the positive threshold voltage V_th.

questions.question: A Zener diode is primarily utilized in electronic circuits for:

options.text: DC voltage regulation in reverse breakdown mode
Half-wave AC rectification in forward bias

questions.explanation: Zener diodes maintain a constant breakdown voltage across their terminals when operated in reverse breakdown, making them ideal voltage references and regulators.

questions.question: According to De Morgan's Laws, the logical expression (A + B)' is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: De Morgan's first theorem states: the complement of a sum is equal to the product of the individual complements: (A + B)' = A' · B'.

questions.question: How many select input lines are required for an 8-to-1 Multiplexer (MUX)?
questions.explanation: For 2^n input data lines, exactly n select lines are needed. 2³ = 8, so n = 3 select lines are required.

questions.question: Which flip-flop has the characteristic equation Q(next) = D, directly capturing the input on the active clock edge?
questions.explanation: The D (Data) flip-flop stores whatever logic level is present on the D line at the clock transition: Q_{next} = D.

questions.question: In a 4-variable Karnaugh Map (K-map), grouping 8 adjacent 1s eliminates how many boolean variables?
questions.explanation: Grouping 2^k adjacent cells in a K-map eliminates k variables. For an octet (8 cells = 2³), 3 variables are eliminated, leaving a single literal term.

questions.question: A continuous-time system defined by y(t) = x(2t) is:
questions.explanation: Time compression x(2t) is linear, but shifting the input by t₀ produces x(2(t - t₀)) ≠ x(2t - t₀), making it time-variant. For t > 0 (e.g. t = 1, y(1) = x(2)), it relies on future input, so it is non-causal.

questions.question: The convolution of any arbitrary signal x(t) with an ideal Dirac unit impulse δ(t - t₀) results in:
questions.explanation: By the sifting property of convolution, convolving any function with a shifted impulse simply shifts the function by that amount: x(t) * δ(t - t₀) = x(t - t₀).

questions.question: An LTI system with impulse response h(t) is Bounded-Input Bounded-Output (BIBO) stable if and only if:

options.text: The Laplace ROC excludes the imaginary axis
The poles are strictly on the unit circle

questions.explanation: BIBO stability of a continuous-time LTI system requires the impulse response to be absolutely integrable.

questions.question: The Fourier Transform of an ideal unit rectangular pulse of width T centered at t = 0 is a:
questions.explanation: The continuous-time Fourier transform of a rectangular pulse rect(t/T) is a standard sinc function in the frequency domain.

questions.question: The closed-loop transfer function T(s) of a unity feedback system with forward path gain G(s) is:
questions.explanation: For negative unity feedback: T(s) = Y(s)/R(s) = G(s) / [1 + G(s)H(s)]. With H(s) = 1, T(s) = G(s) / [1 + G(s)].

questions.question: In a standard second-order system s² + 2ζω_n s + ω_n² = 0, the system is CRITICALLY DAMPED when damping ratio ζ equals:
questions.explanation: Critical damping occurs at the boundary condition ζ = 1, where both closed-loop poles are real and identical.

questions.question: According to the Routh-Hurwitz stability criterion, a closed-loop system is strictly stable if and only if:

options.text: All entries in the first column of the Routh array are strictly positive (no sign changes)
The determinant of the gain matrix is zero
There is at least one sign change in the first row
All roots of the characteristic equation lie in the right-half s-plane

questions.explanation: The number of sign changes in the first column of the Routh array equals the number of roots in the right-half s-plane. Stability requires 0 roots in the RHP, meaning no sign changes.

questions.question: In a PID controller with transfer function C(s) = Kp + Ki/s + Kd*s, what is the primary role of the DERIVATIVE (Kd) action?

options.text: Anticipates future errors and improves system transient response by increasing damping
Reduces steady-state error to zero for step inputs

questions.explanation: Derivative action Kd responds to the rate of error change, introducing lead/damping to decrease oscillations and overshoot.

questions.question: According to the Nyquist Sampling Theorem, to avoid aliasing, a continuous bandlimited signal with maximum frequency f_max must be sampled at a rate fs satisfying:
questions.explanation: The Nyquist rate is the minimum sampling rate f_s = 2 * f_max required to enable perfect signal reconstruction without spectral overlap.

questions.question: In Amplitude Modulation (AM), if the carrier amplitude is 10 V and the modulating message signal amplitude is 6 V, the modulation index μ is:
questions.explanation: The AM modulation index is defined as μ = Am / Ac = 6 V / 10 V = 0.6 (or 60%).

questions.question: The Shannon-Hartley theorem states that the theoretical maximum information capacity C of an AWGN channel with bandwidth B and signal-to-noise ratio SNR is:
questions.explanation: The Shannon channel capacity formula is C = B * log₂(1 + S/N) in bits per second.

questions.question: Which digital modulation technique alters the phase of the carrier signal among 4 discrete constellation states (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°)?
questions.explanation: QPSK modulates 2 bits per symbol into 4 discrete phase states spaced 90° apart.

questions.question: At the network edge, which of the following typically acts as the primary initiators of communication?
questions.explanation: In client-server architecture, client hosts reside at the network edge and actively initiate requests toward servers.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using a full-duplex communication link compared to half-duplex?

options.text: It allows data to be transmitted and received simultaneously.
It reduces the signal strength needed for transmission.
It allows transmission in only one direction at a time.
It decreases the overall frequency bandwidth required.

questions.explanation: Full-duplex channels permit concurrent bidirectional data transmission without collision or turn-taking delays.

questions.question: Which physical transmission media is commonly used in high-speed optical long-haul communication?

options.text: Glass or plastic thin optical fibers

questions.explanation: Fiber-optic cables conduct light pulses through silica fibers, providing extremely high bandwidth and noise immunity.

questions.question: How many total usable host IP addresses are available in an IPv4 subnet with a CIDR prefix of /26?
questions.explanation: A /26 prefix has 32 - 26 = 6 host bits. Total addresses = 2⁶ = 64. Subtracting 2 (network and broadcast addresses) leaves 62 usable host addresses.

questions.question: During TCP connection termination, how many packets (FIN/ACK handshakes) are exchanged in the standard closing sequence?
questions.explanation: TCP uses a 4-way handshake to gracefully tear down both simplex directions of the full-duplex connection.

questions.question: Which cloud computing service model provides customers with raw virtual machines, storage, and network virtualization?
questions.explanation: IaaS delivers fundamental computing infrastructure (virtual servers, storage, networking) upon which clients install and configure their own OS and applications.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Type-1 (bare-metal) Hypervisor and a Type-2 (hosted) Hypervisor?

options.text: Type-1 runs directly on the physical hardware, while Type-2 runs on top of a host operating system.
Type-1 is only for Windows, while Type-2 is for Linux.
Type-2 has lower overhead and higher I/O performance than Type-1.

questions.explanation: Bare-metal hypervisors (Type-1, e.g. VMware ESXi, KVM) execute directly on server hardware without an intermediate host OS.

questions.question: In cloud computing architectures, horizontal scaling (scaling out) refers to:

options.text: Adding more server instances or virtual machines to share the workload
Upgrading the CPU and RAM of an existing single server instance
Migrating workloads from public cloud to private cloud

questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (scale out) adds more parallel nodes/machines to distribute traffic, enabling elasticity and high fault tolerance.

questions.question: Under the Cloud Shared Responsibility Model, which responsibility is ALWAYS the exclusive duty of the cloud customer across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS?

options.text: Data security and customer access management

questions.explanation: Customers are always responsible for managing and protecting their own data, credentials, and access policies regardless of cloud service tier.

questions.question: In AC power analysis, if real power P = 800 W and reactive power Q = 600 VAR (inductive), what is the apparent power |S| and power factor (PF)?
questions.explanation: |S| = √(P² + Q²) = √(800² + 600²) = 1000 VA. Power factor = P / |S| = 800 / 1000 = 0.8 lagging (since Q > 0 is inductive).

questions.question: In a series resonant circuit with R = 10 Ω, L = 100 mH, and C = 10 μF, what is the Quality Factor Q of the circuit?
In a Common-Emitter BJT amplifier, what is the primary effect of adding an unbypassed emitter resistor R_E?

options.text: It stabilizes the voltage gain against temperature and β variations (negative feedback) at the expense of lower gain.
It causes the amplifier to oscillate at high frequencies.
It shifts the operating point into cutoff.
It eliminates all harmonic distortion completely.

questions.explanation: An unbypassed emitter resistor provides negative feedback, stabilizing gain and raising input resistance while reducing total gain magnitude.

questions.question: For an n-channel enhancement MOSFET operating in the SATURATION region, the drain current I_D is related to (V_GS - V_th) by:

options.text: I_D is directly proportional to V_DS linearly

questions.explanation: In saturation (pinch-off), the drain current follows the square-law relationship I_D = 0.5 * k_n * (V_GS - V_th)² and is independent of V_DS to first order.

questions.question: In digital arithmetic, what are the Boolean expressions for the Sum (S) and Carry-Out (C_out) of a Full Adder with inputs A, B, and C_in?

options.text: S = A ⊕ B ⊕ C_in,  C_out = AB + C_in(A ⊕ B)
S = AB + C_in,  C_out = A ⊕ B ⊕ C_in
S = A + B + C_in,  C_out = ABC_in

questions.explanation: The standard full adder produces Sum = A ⊕ B ⊕ C_in and Carry = AB + C_in(A ⊕ B).

questions.question: In a JK Flip-Flop, what is the next state Q(next) when inputs J = 1 and K = 1 at the active clock edge?
questions.explanation: When both J and K are logic 1, the JK flip-flop toggles its output state on every clock pulse.

questions.question: What is the Laplace transform of the causal exponential signal x(t) = e^(-3t) u(t), and what is its Region of Convergence (ROC)?
questions.explanation: ℒ{e^(-at)u(t)} = 1/(s + a) for Re{s} > -a. Here a = 3, so X(s) = 1/(s + 3) with ROC Re{s} > -3.

questions.question: If the Fourier transform of x(t) is X(ω), what is the Fourier transform of the time-shifted signal x(t - t₀)?
questions.explanation: By the time-shifting property of the continuous-time Fourier transform: ℱ{x(t - t₀)} = e^(-j ω t₀) X(ω).

questions.question: For a unity negative feedback system with open-loop transfer function G(s) = 10 / [s(s + 2)(s + 5)], what is the System Type and position error constant Kp?

options.text: Type 1 system with Kp = ∞ (zero steady-state error to step input)

questions.explanation: Since there is one pole at s = 0 (1/s term), it is a Type 1 system. The position error constant Kp = lim_{s→0} G(s) = 10/0 = ∞.

questions.question: In root locus construction, the number of separate root locus branches that terminate at infinity equals:

options.text: n - m (number of poles minus number of finite zeros)

questions.explanation: Root locus branches originate at open-loop poles (n) and terminate at open-loop zeros (m). The remaining n - m branches terminate at infinity along asymptotes.

questions.question: According to Carson's Rule, what is the approximate transmission bandwidth B_T required for a Frequency Modulated (FM) signal with peak frequency deviation Δf and message bandwidth f_m?
questions.explanation: Carson's empirical rule states FM bandwidth B_T ≈ 2(Δf + f_m) = 2 f_m(1 + β).

questions.question: In Pulse Code Modulation (PCM), if each sample is quantized into n bits, increasing n by 1 bit improves the signal-to-quantization-noise ratio (SQNR) by approximately:
questions.explanation: Each additional quantization bit doubles the number of levels (2^n), decreasing noise power by a factor of 4, which translates to a 6.02 dB improvement in SQNR.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural difference between Docker containers and traditional Virtual Machines (VMs)?

options.text: Containers share the host operating system kernel, whereas VMs each run a full guest operating system on top of a hypervisor.
VMs start in milliseconds while containers take minutes.
Containers do not provide filesystem isolation.

questions.explanation: Containers virtualize at the OS level, sharing the underlying host kernel to achieve lightweight footprint and fast startup.

questions.question: In cloud storage terminology, Amazon S3 is an example of what type of storage service?

options.text: Object Storage (REST API accessible via unique URIs)
Block Storage for raw OS disks

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 is a massively scalable object store where data is stored as discrete objects containing metadata and unique identifiers accessed via HTTP.

questions.question: When measuring an unknown electric current with a digital multimeter (DMM), how must the multimeter be inserted into the circuit?

options.text: In series with the component whose current is being measured
Connected directly between power supply terminals
Connected to the ground probe only

questions.explanation: Current flows through the meter, so the ammeter must be inserted in series, presenting very low internal impedance.

questions.question: On an oscilloscope display, if a sinusoidal waveform occupies 4 vertical divisions at 2 V/div, what is its peak-to-peak voltage (V_pp)?
questions.explanation: Peak-to-peak voltage V_pp = (Number of vertical divisions) * (Volts/Div) = 4 div * 2 V/div = 8 V.

questions.question: In an experimental RC transient circuit, the time constant τ is determined as the time required for capacitor voltage to charge to approximately what percentage of its final DC value?
When determining the Thevenin equivalent experimentally in the lab, the open-circuit voltage Voc = 12 V and short-circuit current Isc = 3 mA are measured. What is Rth?
questions.explanation: By Ohm's law, Rth = Voc / Isc = 12 V / 0.003 A = 4000 Ω = 4 kΩ.

questions.question: In the digital logic laboratory, which standard 74xx TTL integrated circuit provides four 2-input Quad NAND gates?
questions.explanation: The 7400 is the industry-standard Quad 2-input NAND gate IC.

questions.question: Refer to the test setup diagram shown below. Identify the circuit function implemented by the multiplexer configuration:
questions.explanation: The circuit diagram demonstrates standard multiplexer data routing where select input S steers channel A or channel B to output F.

questions.question: Which standard TTL IC is a 3-to-8 line decoder with active-low outputs commonly used in memory address decoding experiments?
questions.explanation: The 74138 is a 3-to-8 decoder with active-low outputs and multiple enable pins.

questions.question: Refer to the circuit schematic shown below. Analyze the decoder outputs connected to the active-low OR gate to determine the final minimized SOP function F:
questions.explanation: Connecting active-low minterm outputs of a decoder to a NAND or negative-input OR gate directly forms the standard Sum-Of-Products logic function.

questions.question: When verifying silicon diode characteristics on an oscilloscope, what is the observed forward voltage drop (knee voltage) at moderate forward currents?
questions.explanation: Standard silicon diodes exhibit an approximate 0.7 V turn-on barrier voltage in lab measurements.

questions.question: In a bridge rectifier lab experiment with an AC input of 12 V_rms, what is the approximate peak DC output voltage across the load (accounting for diode drops)?
questions.explanation: V_peak = 12 * √2 ≈ 16.97 V. In a bridge rectifier, two diodes conduct simultaneously: V_out_peak = 16.97 - 2(0.7) = 15.57 V ≈ 15.6 V.

questions.question: In a Common-Emitter BJT amplifier circuit, what is the phase relationship between the input AC voltage signal and the output AC voltage signal at the collector?
questions.explanation: Common-Emitter amplifiers produce an inherent 180° phase inversion between base AC input and collector AC output.

questions.question: When measuring the ripple voltage of a power supply filter capacitor with an oscilloscope, the oscilloscope input coupling switch should be set to:

options.text: AC Coupling (blocks DC component to view small ripple amplitude)

questions.explanation: AC coupling blocks large DC average voltages, allowing the oscilloscope vertical gain to be increased to measure millivolt ripple accurately.

questions.question: In C++, what is the correct syntax to allocate a new node with data value 42 on the heap for a singly linked list?
questions.explanation: Heap allocation in modern C++ uses the new operator returning a pointer to the newly constructed object.

questions.question: When evaluating the postfix arithmetic expression "5 3 + 2 *" using a stack, what is the final calculated value?
questions.explanation: Push 5, Push 3. Encounter '+': pop 3 and 5, push 5+3=8. Push 2. Encounter '*': pop 2 and 8, push 8*2=16.

questions.question: What is the correct base condition in a recursive function to compute the height of a Binary Search Tree (BST) when root is NULL?
questions.explanation: Empty tree base case returns -1 (for edge-based height) or 0 (for node-based height).

questions.question: In a circular array implementation of a queue with capacity 8, if front = 4 and rear = 2, how many elements are currently in the queue?
questions.explanation: Count = (rear - front + capacity) % capacity = (2 - 4 + 8) % 8 = 6 elements.

questions.question: In 8086 DOS programming, which DOS interrupt service is invoked to print a '$'-terminated string located at DX to the console?
questions.explanation: DOS service AH = 09h of INT 21h prints a string whose offset is in DX, terminated by '$'.

questions.question: Which instruction sequence properly terminates an assembly program and returns control cleanly to the DOS command prompt?
questions.explanation: Function 4Ch of INT 21h exits with return code (AL), cleanly terminating execution.

questions.question:
What is the content of AL after executing the following instructions?

MOV AL, 5
ADD AL, 3
SUB AL, 2
In an assembly array summation routine, which register is commonly used as a pointer/index into memory elements in x86?
questions.explanation: ESI and EDI are standard 32-bit index registers designed for string and memory array traversals.

questions.question: In processor simulation tools (like Logisim or ModelSim), what is the function of a Program Counter (PC)?

options.text: A register that holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched and executed
An accumulator that stores ALU results
A stack pointer for function returns

questions.explanation: The Program Counter holds the memory address of the next instruction in sequence.

questions.question: In a single-cycle MIPS datapath simulation, how many clock cycles does each instruction take to execute?
questions.explanation: In a single-cycle datapath, the clock cycle period is fixed to accommodate the slowest instruction, taking exactly 1 long cycle per instruction.

questions.question: In a 4-bit ALU simulation, which control signal typically selects between addition and subtraction?

options.text: Invert B input and set Carry-In Cin = 1 (2's complement subtraction)

questions.explanation: Subtraction A - B is computed as A + (~B) + 1, implemented by inverting B and setting Cin = 1.

questions.question: When designing an Instruction Memory module in logic simulators, the memory address input is typically connected directly to:
questions.explanation: Instruction fetch requires providing the PC value as the address input to Instruction Memory.

questions.question: When using a Vernier caliper, if the main scale reads 12 mm and the 6th Vernier division aligns (with resolution 0.05 mm), what is the total measured reading?
questions.explanation: Reading = Main Scale + (Aligned Division * Resolution) = 12 mm + (6 * 0.05 mm) = 12 mm + 0.30 mm = 12.30 mm.

questions.question: In the simple pendulum lab experiment, what is the formula relating the period T to pendulum length L and gravitational acceleration g?
questions.explanation: The period of a simple pendulum for small oscillations is T = 2π √(L/g).

questions.question: In a force table experiment, three concurrent coplanar forces are in static equilibrium. The vector sum of the three forces must equal:
questions.explanation: Static equilibrium requires the net vector sum of all forces acting at the center ring to be identically zero: ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0.

questions.question: When plotting T² (period squared) versus L (pendulum length), the resulting graph is a straight line whose slope is equal to:
questions.explanation: Squaring T = 2π√(L/g) gives T² = (4π²/g) * L. Thus the slope is 4π²/g.

questions.question: In an acid-base titration experiment, what indicator is commonly used to observe the endpoint transition between colorless in acid and pink in basic solution?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is clear in acidic and neutral solutions and turns distinct pink around pH 8.2–10.0.

questions.question: Which volumetric glassware provides the highest volumetric precision for dispensing variable volumes of titrant liquid?
questions.explanation: A burette is calibrated to dispense finely controlled volumes with readability up to ±0.01 mL.

questions.question: In a titration, 25.0 mL of unknown HCl is neutralized by 20.0 mL of 0.100 M NaOH standard solution. What is the molarity of the HCl solution?
questions.explanation: M_acid * V_acid = M_base * V_base => M_acid * 25.0 mL = 0.100 M * 20.0 mL => M_acid = 2.00 / 25.0 = 0.080 M.

questions.question: When heating crucible contents using a Bunsen burner in an empirical formula experiment, the crucible lid is kept slightly ajar in order to:

options.text: Allow oxygen to enter while preventing ash and oxide smoke from escaping
Accelerate evaporation of the porcelain material
Prevent condensation on the clay triangle

questions.explanation: Ajar lid allows atmospheric oxygen into the crucible to oxidize magnesium while containing spattering and oxide particulates.

questions.question: In MATLAB/Simulink control system modeling, which built-in function creates a continuous-time transfer function object from numerator and denominator polynomial vectors?
questions.explanation: tf(num, den) creates a transfer function model in MATLAB (e.g. sys = tf([1], [1, 2, 1])).

questions.question: When analyzing a second-order underdamped step response in the lab, the Peak Time (Tp) is observed at 0.5 s. The damped natural frequency ω_d is:
questions.explanation: Peak time formula is Tp = π / ω_d => ω_d = π / Tp = π / 0.5 = 2π rad/s.

questions.question: In MATLAB control system toolbox, which command generates the root locus plot of a linear open-loop system?
questions.explanation: The rlocus(sys) command computes and plots the trajectories of the closed-loop poles as gain K varies from 0 to infinity.

questions.question: On a Bode plot generated in MATLAB, Phase Margin (PM) is measured at the frequency where the open-loop magnitude curve crosses:
questions.explanation: Phase margin is defined as PM = 180° + ∠G(jω_gc) evaluated at the gain crossover frequency where |G(jω)| = 0 dB (gain of 1).

questions.question: ما هو المصدر الأول والأساسي للتشريع الإسلامي والثقافة الإسلامية؟

questions.question: ما هو المفهوم الذي يُعبر عن الرابطة القانونية والسياسية والمعنوية بين الفرد والدولة وما يترتب عليها من حقوق وواجبات؟

questions.question: الحق الحصري القانوني الممنوح لمخترع لمنع الآخرين من صنع أو استخدام أو بيع اختراعه لمدة زمنية محددة يسمى:
questions.explanation: براءة الاختراع هي وثيقة حماية ملكية صناعية رسمية تمنح للمخترع حقاً استئثارياً لمدة غالباً 20 عاماً مقابل الكشف عن الاختراع.

questions.question: المصطلح الذي يشير إلى أدنى نموذج لمنتج يحتوي على الخصائص الأساسية التي تسمح بجمعه لاختبار ردود فعل العملاء الحقيقيين وتطويره يسمى:
questions.explanation: MVP (Minimum Viable Product) هو نموذج أولي يضم الخصائص الأساسية لاختبار فرضيات السوق بأقل جهد وتكلفة.

questions.question: في مشغل التمديدات الكهربائية، ما هو الغرض الأساسي من استخدام سلك التأريض (Ground Wire) في الدوائر والأجهزة الكهربائية؟

questions.question: أهم وسيلة وقاية شخصية يجب ارتداؤها بشكل إلزامي في جميع المشاغل والورش الهندسية لحماية القدمين من سقوط الأجسام الحادة والثقيلة هي:

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence that observes subject-verb agreement:

options.text: Neither the professor nor the students were in the laboratory.
Neither the professor nor the students was in the laboratory.
Neither the professor nor the students is in the laboratory.
Neither the professor or the students has been in the lab.

questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by "neither... nor", the verb agrees with the closer subject ("students", which is plural, taking "were").

questions.question: Identify the passive voice transformation of: "The engineer inspected the transmission towers yesterday."

options.text: The transmission towers were inspected by the engineer yesterday.
The transmission towers was inspected yesterday by the engineer.
The engineer was inspecting the transmission towers yesterday.
The transmission towers have been inspected by the engineer.

questions.explanation: Past simple passive voice follows: Object + was/were + past participle (inspected) + by agent.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a dangling modifier that needs correction?

options.text: Walking into the server room, the temperature felt freezing.
Walking into the server room, the technician felt freezing.
The technician felt the freezing temperature upon entering the server room.
As the technician entered the room, it felt freezing.

questions.explanation: In option A, the participial phrase "Walking into the server room" illogically modifies "the temperature" instead of the human subject.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a "Topic Sentence" in an academic paragraph?

options.text: It states the central controlling idea of the paragraph that all supporting sentences elaborate on.

questions.explanation: The topic sentence explicitly states the main point or governing idea developed by the subsequent supporting evidence.

questions.question: Which transitional phrase is best suited to introduce a contrasting academic perspective?
questions.explanation: "However" and "On the other hand" signal contrast or counter-argument between viewpoints.

questions.question: What constitutes "Plagiarism" in scholarly and academic writing?

options.text: Using another author's ideas, words, or data without proper citation or acknowledgment.
Writing a comprehensive bibliography in APA format.
Synthesizing ideas from multiple peer-reviewed papers.

questions.explanation: Plagiarism is presenting someone else's intellectual work or words as your own without adequate attribution.

questions.question: In a formal argumentative essay, the "Counter-argument" section serves to:

options.text: Acknowledge an opposing viewpoint and provide evidence to refute or concede it, strengthening overall credibility.
Contradict the author's main thesis statement completely.
Repeat the abstract in simpler words.

questions.explanation: Addressing counter-arguments demonstrates thoroughness, objectivity, and directly reinforces the paper's thesis through effective rebuttal.

questions.question: Which style of language is inappropriate in formal engineering research papers?

options.text: Colloquial slang and informal contractions (e.g., "don't", "gonna", "cool stuff")
Precise quantitative measurements with SI units
Standard technical terminology and clear diagrams

questions.explanation: Academic writing strictly avoids casual idioms, personal emotional appeals, and contractions.

questions.question: In an engineering project report, what is the primary purpose of the "Executive Summary"?

options.text: To provide a concise overview of the problem, methodology, key findings, and recommendations for decision-makers.
To list the names and phone numbers of the team members.

questions.explanation: An executive summary provides busy managers with a standalone synopsis of objectives, results, and critical decisions.

questions.question: What is the correct convention for labeling figures and tables in formal IEEE engineering documents?

options.text: Figure captions placed below figures; Table captions placed above tables.
Figure captions placed above; Table captions below.
Captions placed only in the appendix.
No captions needed if discussed in body text.

questions.explanation: Standard IEEE and technical formatting rules place Table titles above the table, and Figure captions beneath the figure.

questions.question: Which section of a technical report describes the step-by-step procedures, equipment models, and experimental setups used?
questions.explanation: The Methodology details instruments, protocols, and designs to ensure results are replicable by other engineers.

questions.question: In professional technical correspondence (such as engineering emails), the subject line should be:

A single generic word like "Hello" or "Help"

questions.question: If $1,000 is invested today at an annual compound interest rate of 10%, what is its future worth (F) at the end of 2 years?

questions.explanation: The Time Value of Money is the cornerstone of engineering economics, reflecting earning capacity and inflation over time.

questions.question: In capital budgeting, the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) is defined as the discount rate at which:

options.text: The Net Present Value (NPV) of the project cash flows equals exactly zero
The total future value is doubled
The payback period equals one fiscal year

questions.explanation: The IRR is the exact discount interest rate that equates the present value of cash inflows to initial investment outflows (NPV = 0).

questions.question: A machine with initial cost $50,000 has an estimated salvage value of $10,000 after 5 years. Using Straight-Line depreciation, what is the annual depreciation charge?
questions.explanation: Annual Straight-Line depreciation = (Initial Cost - Salvage Value) / Useful Life = ($50,000 - $10,000) / 5 = $40,000 / 5 = $8,000/year.

questions.question: ما هما الشرطان الأساسيان المتفق عليهما شرعاً لقبول أي عمل صالح عند الله تعالى؟

questions.question: ما هي الهيئة المستقلة التي أنشئت في الأردن بموجب التعديلات الدستورية لإدارة العمليات الانتخابية والنيابية والإشراف عليها؟

questions.question: شارك اللواء المدرع الأربعين الأردني (لواء الله) ببطولة وشجاعة في الدفاع عن الأراضي العربية على الجبهة السورية في حرب:
questions.explanation: خاض اللواء المدرع الأربعين الأردني معارك ضارية على هضبة الجولان عام 1973 ومنع القوات الإسرائيلية من التقدم نحو دمشق.

questions.question: ما هو الفرع أو السلاح العسكري في الجيش العربي المسؤول عن الاتصالات ونقل المعلومات وتأمين القيادة والسيطرة وإدارة الحرب الإلكترونية؟
questions.explanation: سلاح اللاسلكي والاتصالات مسؤول عن تأمين كافة شبكات الاتصال السلكية واللاسلكية والأمن السيبراني العسكري.

questions.question: الوثيقة التاريخية الخالدة التي منحها الخليفة عمر بن الخطاب لأهل إيلياء (القدس) عام 15 هـ لضمان أمن كنائسهم وأموالهم وأنفسهم تسمى:
questions.explanation: العهدة العمرية هي وثيقة الأمان والتسامح الديني التي كتبها الخليفة عمر بن الخطاب لأهل القدس عندما فتحها المسلمون سلماً سنة 15 هـ.

questions.question: من هو العالم المسلم الموسوعي الذي أسس علم الجبر وألف كتاب "المختصر في حساب الجبر والمقابلة" وتُنسب إليه الخوارزميات (Algorithms)؟
questions.explanation: الخوارزمي هو مؤسس علم الجبر واستخدم النظام العشري والصفر، ومن اسمه اشتُق مصطلح الخوارزميات (Algorithm) في علوم الحاسوب.

questions.question: في التحليل الاستراتيجي للمشاريع الريادية المعروف بـ (SWOT Analysis)، يرمز حرفا (S) و (W) إلى العوامل:

questions.question: التمويل الذي يقدمه مستثمرون متخصصون لشركات تكنولوجية ناشئة ذات إمكانات نمو هائلة مقابل حصة ملكية في الشركة يسمى:

questions.question: أي نوع من طفايات الحريق هو الأنسب والأكثر أماناً لإخماد الحرائق الناتجة عن الأجهزة الكهربائية والتمديدات في المشاغل دون التسبب بصعق كهربائي؟

options.text: طفاية غاز ثاني أكسيد الكربون (CO₂) أو البودرة الجافة
