questions.explanation: Collector current I_C = beta * I_B = 100 * 15 uA = 1.50 mA. By KVL around collector loop: V_CE = V_CC - I_C * R_C = 15 - (1.50 * 1.0) = 13.50 V.

questions.question: At the network edge, which of the following typically acts as the primary initiators of communication?
questions.explanation: In the client-server architecture, client hosts (desktop, laptops, smartphones) reside at the network edge and actively initiate requests toward servers.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using a full-duplex communication link compared to half-duplex?

options.text: It allows data to be transmitted and received simultaneously.
It reduces the signal strength needed for transmission.
It allows transmission in only one direction at a time.
It decreases the overall frequency bandwidth required.

questions.explanation: Full-duplex channels permit concurrent bidirectional data transmission without collision or turn-taking delays.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a server in a network?

options.text: It primarily initiates communication with clients.
It typically provides resources or services to clients.
It is usually capable of handling multiple requests simultaneously.
It often resides in a data center for scalability and availability.

questions.explanation: Servers passively listen for incoming requests; clients are the entities that initiate the communication.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the client-server model in networking?

options.text: Every device acts as both client and server symmetrically.
A model where clients request services and always-on servers respond with requested resources.
A model requiring peer-to-peer decentralized file swapping.
A model where clients provide services directly to servers.

questions.explanation: The client-server architecture features an always-on host (server) servicing requests from dynamically connecting clients.

questions.question: Which physical transmission media is commonly used in high-speed fiber-optic communication?
questions.explanation: Fiber-optic cables conduct light pulses through ultra-pure glass or silica fibers, providing extremely high bandwidth and immunity to electromagnetic interference.

questions.question: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of circuit switching (used in traditional telephone networks)?

options.text: Data is broken into independent packets sent over shared paths.
A dedicated, end-to-end physical path is established for the entire session duration.
Resources are allocated on demand dynamically using statistical multiplexing.
It is optimized for bursty Internet web browsing traffic.

questions.explanation: Circuit switching pre-reserves end-to-end transmission capacity (frequency/time slots) exclusively for the session duration.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)?

options.text: To encrypt data between web browsers and servers
To route IP packets across the internet core
To enable communication and resource transfer between web browsers and web servers
To assign dynamic IP addresses automatically to hosts

questions.explanation: HTTP is the application-layer protocol powering the World Wide Web, standardizing how clients request objects and how servers deliver web pages.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code indicates a successful request where the server returns the requested resource?
questions.explanation: HTTP status 200 represents standard successful transaction completion.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural difference between POP3 and IMAP mail access protocols?

options.text: POP3 stores emails on the client side after downloading, while IMAP maintains folder synchronization on the remote server.
IMAP removes emails from the server, while POP3 keeps them organized remotely.
IMAP is used for sending emails, while POP3 is for receiving.
POP3 requires encryption, while IMAP cannot use SSL/TLS.

questions.explanation: POP3 follows download-and-delete or download-and-keep mode locally, whereas IMAP keeps full email state and folders synchronized on the mail server.

questions.question: Which protocol is primarily used by mail clients to send outgoing email messages to a mail server?
questions.explanation: SMTP is a push protocol specifically designed to transmit email messages from sender client to mail server, and between mail servers.

questions.question: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of UDP (User Datagram Protocol)?

options.text: Lightweight connectionless delivery suitable for real-time video streaming, DNS, and gaming

questions.explanation: UDP provides minimal transport overhead without connection establishment delays or retransmissions, making it ideal for delay-sensitive real-time traffic.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Domain Name System (DNS)?

options.text: To encrypt web traffic over HTTPS
To translate human-friendly domain names (e.g. example.com) into numerical IP addresses
To establish VPN tunnels between remote sites
To allocate dynamic MAC addresses to routers

questions.explanation: DNS serves as the distributed directory of the Internet, resolving hostname strings into 32-bit (IPv4) or 128-bit (IPv6) addresses.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI 7-layer reference model is responsible for reliable end-to-end process-to-process communication?
questions.explanation: The Transport layer (Layer 4) manages end-to-end logical communication between running application processes on different hosts.

questions.question: In transport layer protocols (TCP and UDP), what is the function of a "Port Number"?

options.text: A 16-bit identifier used to direct incoming segment data to a specific socket/process on the host
The physical Ethernet port jack on the router
The MAC address of the network interface card
The transmission baud rate of the communication cable

questions.explanation: Port numbers (0 to 65535) allow multiplexing and demultiplexing, differentiating between concurrent network applications running on the same host.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 3-Way Handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) in TCP?

options.text: To establish a synchronized, reliable connection and agree on initial sequence numbers before transmitting data
To encrypt packets using symmetric keys
To calculate the shortest path across the core routers
To terminate an idle socket connection

questions.explanation: The 3-way handshake ensures both parties confirm mutual reachability and synchronize starting sequence numbers.

questions.question: When TCP detects packet loss or network congestion, how does its congestion control algorithm respond?

options.text: It aggressively increases cwnd to push remaining packets
It reduces the Congestion Window (cwnd) size and slows down transmission rate
It switches from TCP to UDP automatically
It ignores packet drops and relies on physical hardware

questions.explanation: TCP infers network congestion from timeout or duplicate ACKs, dropping its cwnd to prevent router buffer collapse.

questions.question: Given that ∫ₐᵇ f(x) sin²x dx = 5 and ∫ₐᵇ f(x) cos²x dx = 7, then ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx =
questions.explanation: By linearity of the integral: ∫ₐᵇ f(x)(sin²x + cos²x) dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(x)*1 dx = 5 + 7 = 12.

questions.question: Find the second derivative: (d²/dx²)(x³ + x² + 2) =
questions.explanation: First derivative is 3x² + 2x. Second derivative is d/dx (3x² + 2x) = 6x + 2.

questions.question: Evaluate the definite integral: ∫₀⁴ [x / √(x² + 1)] dx =
questions.explanation: Let u = x² + 1, du = 2x dx. When x = 0, u = 1; when x = 4, u = 17. The integral becomes (1/2) ∫₁¹⁷ u^(-1/2) du = [u^(1/2)]₁¹⁷ = √17 - 1.

questions.question: The area of the region in the first quadrant, which is bounded by the coordinate axes and the curve of the function f(x) = cos(x) is equal to:
questions.explanation: In the first quadrant, cos(x) is bounded between x = 0 and x = π/2. Area = ∫₀^(π/2) cos(x) dx = [sin(x)]₀^(π/2) = sin(π/2) - sin(0) = 1 square unit.

questions.question: The arc length of the curve of the function f(x) = 2√(x³) + 1 from x = 0 to x = 1 is:
The relative minimum of the function f(x) = (1/3)x³ - 3x² + 5x + 10 occurs when x =
questions.explanation: f'(x) = x² - 6x + 5 = (x - 1)(x - 5) = 0 => critical points x = 1, 5. f''(x) = 2x - 6. f''(1) = -4 < 0 (local max), f''(5) = 4 > 0 (local min). Hence relative minimum occurs at x = 5.

questions.question: If f(x) = csc⁻¹(x), then f(3) is equal to:
questions.explanation: By the standard inverse trigonometric identity, csc⁻¹(x) = sin⁻¹(1/x) for |x| ≥ 1. Therefore, f(3) = sin⁻¹(1/3).

questions.question: If f(x) = x² + 4x + 7 for x ∈ (-∞, k] is a one-to-one function, then the largest possible value of k is:
questions.explanation: The parabola f(x) has its vertex at x = -b / (2a) = -4 / 2 = -2. It is monotonic on (-∞, -2] and [-2, ∞). For x ∈ (-∞, k] to be one-to-one, k cannot exceed the vertex at -2.

questions.question: Evaluate the limit: lim_{x → 3} [ 1 / (x - 3) - 27 / (x³ - 27) ] =
If y = 0 and x = 2 are horizontal and vertical asymptotes (respectively) of the function f(x) = [ax³ - x(3x + 1)] / [x³ - b], then a + b =
questions.explanation: For horizontal asymptote y = 0: degree of numerator must be less than denominator, so a = 0. For vertical asymptote at x = 2: x³ - b = 0 at x = 2 => 2³ - b = 0 => b = 8. Thus a + b = 0 + 8 = 8.

questions.question: Determine the parity of the function f(x) = x³ ln|x|:

options.text: negative for all x in domain

questions.explanation: f(-x) = (-x)³ ln|-x| = -x³ ln|x| = -f(x). Since f(-x) = -f(x), the function is odd.

questions.question: In a resistive ladder network, 12 Ω is in parallel with 6 Ω, in series with 16 Ω, in parallel with 5 Ω, in series with 8 Ω, in parallel with 12 Ω. Find the equivalent resistance Req:
For the same resistive network powered by a 30 A current source across terminals a-b, find the voltage across the 8 Ω resistor:
questions.explanation: Total current splits equally between the 12Ω branches (15 A each). The current passing through the 8Ω resistor is 15 A. Voltage = 15 A * 8 Ω = 120 V.

questions.question: How many joules of energy will a 10 Ω resistor connected across a 15 V battery dissipate in 1 minute?
The power of 2,000,000,000 W can be expressed in engineering prefix powers of 10 as:
How many coulombs of charge flow through a circuit carrying a current of 10 A in 1 minute?
The maximum current that a 2 W, 80 kΩ resistor can safely conduct is:
The maximum power that can be delivered to the load resistor R connected between terminals a-b is:
questions.explanation: Pmax occurs when RL = Rth = 2 Ω: Pmax = (Vth)² / (4 * Rth) = (6)² / (4 * 2) = 36 / 8 = 4.5 W.

questions.question: A 30 mH inductor circuit has a switch closed at t = 0. The final steady-state inductor current i(t = ∞) is found to be:
questions.explanation: Under DC steady-state, an inductor behaves as a short circuit. The equivalent circuit analysis produces i(∞) = 2 A.

For the same parallel RLC circuit (L = 1 H, C = 10 mF), find the undamped resonant frequency ω₀:

questions.explanation: Since α = 26 > ω₀ = 10, the roots of the characteristic equation are real and distinct (s1, s2), meaning the circuit is overdamped.
